title: Zoneless Angular & Change Detection
exp: Angular is evolving away from Zone.js. Master provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection() and signal-based change detection.
pts: **Zone.js Overhead:** monkey-patching browser async APIs (`setTimeout`, `Promise`, `addEventListener`) causes global change detection cycles.
**Zoneless Angular:** `provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection()` reduces bundle size and eliminates unnecessary dirty checking.
**Signal-driven updates:** component trees update precisely at signal consumer nodes without checking un-impacted branches.
**RxJS Interop:** `toSignal()` converts Observables to Signals; `toObservable()` converts Signals to Observables.
pr: Migrate a sample app to zoneless change detection
Benchmark change detection cycles with Zoneless vs Zone.js

r: Deep mechanics of Zoneless Angular & Change Detection under concurrent execution.
Always design for idempotency, cancellation propagation, and thread safety.
Memory allocation spikes or CPU bound thread starvation.
Use profiling tools to measure actual baseline allocation before optimizing.
Balancing developer velocity with operational maintenance complexity.
Favor simple, well-tested modular architectures over premature complexity.

qa.q: How does Zoneless Angular alter change detection execution?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** In Zoneless mode, Angular no longer listens to Zone.js async events. Change detection triggers strictly when a Signal value changes, when ChangeDetectorRef.markForCheck() is called, or when an async pipe emits, boosting performance dramatically.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Angular Signals maintain an internal reactive dependency graph (ReactiveNode). When a signal value updates, it marks dependent computed nodes as stale without running change detection immediately. Evaluation happens lazily when read, updating only impacted DOM bindings.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Writing to signals inside an effect() can trigger infinite reactive loops or untracked state dependencies. Fix: use computed() or linkedSignal() for derived state sync, keeping effect() strictly for un-tracked side effects like logging or localStorage.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Signals provide fine-grained, synchronous reactivity without Zone.js overhead, but require learning new primitives (input(), output(), model()) compared to classic RxJS BehaviorSubjects.

qa.q: What caution must you take when using toSignal() with an RxJS Observable?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** toSignal() subscribes immediately upon invocation and unsubscribes when the injection context is destroyed. If the Observable emits an error or completes before initialization, you must handle initialValue or requireSync options carefully.
